methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: A deliberate regional initiative to evaluate AI adoption signals potential for distributed capability building outside the NoVA corridor, but success depends on whether this translates to deep institutional capacity or remains at the planning/awareness level.

signals.title: Virginia Tech outlines philosophy for AI adoption - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's institutional AI philosophy could serve as a distribution mechanism for deep capability across regions where VT has presence (Blacksburg, Roanoke, Richmond), potentially seeding peer learning networks beyond concentrated metro hubs.

signals.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia — site to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development. - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Amazon scrapping four NoVA data centers due to local backlash reveals infrastructure concentration limits, but without corresponding capability distribution elsewhere, this simply constrains growth rather than redistributing AI development opportunity.

signals.title: Virginia governor orders statewide plan to address AI cyberattacks - StateScoop
signals.signal_reading: A statewide cybersecurity mandate for AI attacks suggests platform-level, top-down adoption across all state agencies—potentially creating broad but shallow AI security awareness without building deep technical capability at regional levels.

signals.title: Lawyers need AI education, not AI legislation - Virginia Lawyers Weekly
signals.signal_reading: Legal profession's emphasis on AI education over legislation signals recognition that deep fluency, not just tool access, matters—but whether this educational capacity distributes beyond Richmond/NoVA legal hubs will determine if it reinforces or counters concentration.
